_: Every test.skip() in e2e/race is registered here, and scripts/check-race-skips.mjs refuses one that is not. A `title` is the case's full name — every describe title down to the leaf, joined with ' > ' — because a leaf title alone can name two different cases. That is not unique either, so the checker refuses a name matching more than one collected case rather than counting it once. An entry either names the test that keeps its reason true (`guardedBy` — that test failing or disappearing is how the reason's expiry surfaces), or states in `unguarded` that nothing does and what observation would settle it. The prose reason stays in the comment beside the skip; what is here is the link a reader cannot make by eye.

collect._: A FLOOR on what --project=race collects, per file. Everything else in this ledger asks about the cases Playwright did collect, so a case that stops being collected is invisible to it: short of a total collection failure, deleting a case or a whole file leaves every other assertion satisfied and check:skips green. A minimum rather than an exact count — adding cases must not be a chore, and what this guards against is loss. check-race-skips.mjs prints every file that has grown past its floor, in this shape, so raising one deliberately is a copy-paste.

skips.title: T3b undo > a sampleRate-touching entry is refused while live
skips.unguarded: The reason is that no sampleRate entry can exist while live: the rate picker is disabled from the session start (pinned by 'the live session > locks the model picker and the other device actions for its duration' in src/main.device.test.ts) and the readback re-authors the plan. The refusal that would fire IF such an entry existed is pinned too ('refusals > refuses a rate change while a live session holds the rate' in src/ui/history.test.ts) — but that test sets rateLocked itself, so it asserts the branch and not the unreachability, and naming it as the guard here said the reason was held when it was not. What NOTHING holds is the step between them: that the readback path actually calls reset. An attempt to pin that from the app entry was withdrawn on 2026-08-13 after instrumentation showed it vacuous — the only observable outside a trace build (set_edit_menu_state) reports canUndo from an OPEN, uncommitted entry while the stack stays at u=0 r=0, so deleting rerenderPlan's reset changes nothing the test can see. The measurement is in reference/work/e2e-flakes.md. What would settle it: an observable that separates a committed entry from an open one — the depth already on the VITE_TRACE probe — or a unit test over PlanHistory asserting reset() drops both stacks, together with a reading that the fetch path reaches it.

skips.title: T3b undo > a cancelled Fetch re-points the MIDI bound cache
skips.unguarded: Not a claim about the app, and now not a reachable one either: the case is titled after a path that is gone. A cancelled Fetch used to restore a pre-read clone outside loadPlan; the read runs against a private copy now and the module plan object is never replaced (main.ts), while loadPlan — the one replacement left — announces itself. What survives is the memo's identity backstop, pinned by 'MidiControl > re-points the bound cache when the document is replaced under it' in src/ui/midi.test.ts; that test guards the backstop, NOT this case, which is why it is not named as the guard here. Listed so the count of unwritten cases stays countable. What would settle it: deciding whether to retitle the case around a replacement that can still happen, or delete it — an unwritten case for a path with no producer is a floor entry nobody can ever raise.

skips.title: T8 stress > a thirty-minute session leaks no subscription, timer or plan
skips.unguarded: Recorded in docs/{en,ja}/live-race-harness.md as a known gap: the assertions need module-scope state that none of the harness's four surfaces carries. Costed on 2026-08-13 rather than left as a wish. Undo depth is ALREADY on the VITE_TRACE probe (trace-probe.ts's depth()); the MIDI bound-cache size is a Map on MidiControl and would be one hook; a subscription count is one counter in the control layer; armed timers would need the probe to wrap setTimeout/setInterval at boot, which is contained because the probe only exists in a trace build. The fifth — how many Plan objects a writer can still reach — needs a forced collection, and CDP's HeapProfiler.collectGarbage provides one without any launch flag (this suite already opens a newCDPSession, see e2e/midi.spec.ts), so a WeakRef count or Runtime.queryObjects is reachable in the Chromium-only race project. ⚠️ An earlier version of this entry called that impossible; it was not measured and was wrong. So all five readings are within reach and this is work rather than a dead end — what it is not is small: five readings, a probe surface for four of them, and a duration to choose.
